meta.title: linter: implement pattern-based Jest validation following Vitest approach for binary size optimization
meta.body_summary: Replace static Jest validation arrays with pattern-based validation and unify Jest/Vitest validation using a single is_valid_test_fn_call function to reduce linter binary size.

perf_labels.notes: Copilot iterated from complete removal to pattern-based validation per Dunqing's guidance but the PR was closed without merge, likely due to unresolved correctness concerns or maintainer dissatisfaction with the final approach.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 1976 changed lines, this is a medium-to-large refactor across linter utilities, mostly deletions from removing static validation strings. It targets binary size reduction but was closed without merge despite multiple iterations.

review_details.concern_detail: Dunqing rejected complete removal of VALID_JEST_FN_CALL_CHAINS because it would allow invalid Jest chaining patterns; mandated implementing pattern-based validation as in PR #11384.
review_details.performance_claim: Binary size reduction by eliminating static validation strings and using algorithmic pattern validation, with potential memory efficiency from static arrays.
review_details.rejection_signals: Maintainer Dunqing explicitly rejected complete removal approach; after multiple iterations and feedback, PR was closed without merge, suggesting the final implementation still did not fully satisfy maintainer requirements.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Complex Rust optimization involving pattern-based validation and binary size reduction; Copilot iterated multiple strategies but struggled to meet maintainer's specific approach requirements.

detection_detail.code_reading: Dunqing and Boshen reviewed the code and requirements, provided inline feedback rejecting complete removal and directing the agent towards pattern-based validation.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No binary size measurements or benchmarks provided; the PR only claims binary size reduction without evidence.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: After CHANGES_REQUESTED and multiple iterations, the PR was closed without merge; no further fixes.

core_change_summary.description: Replaced static array VALID_JEST_FN_CALL_CHAINS with a pattern-based validation function is_valid_jest_call that algorithmically checks allowed function call chains and modifiers. Later extended to unify Jest and Vitest validation into a single is_valid_test_fn_call function, removing 1300+ lines of Vitest static arrays.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: const-to-static array changes were made and later reverted; most deletions came from removing validation arrays.
change_trajectory: Initial commit optimized Jest call chains storage to reduce binary size.
Complete removal of Jest validation array after maintainer suggestion.
Re-added pattern-based Jest validation after feedback on invalid patterns.
Const-to-static array changes made then later reverted.
Merged Jest and Vitest validation into unified pattern-based function.

review_signals.summary: Rejected complete removal of validation array because it would allow invalid Jest patterns; requested pattern-based validation as in PR #11384.
Asked to evaluate feasibility of complete removal and to change const to static arrays; later asked to rebase and remove const-to-static changes.
review_signals.action_taken: Copilot attempted complete removal and then reverted const-to-static changes.

review_signals.summary: Asked to unify Jest and Vitest validation into a single function.
Confirmed implementation of pattern-based validation and unified approach.

collaboration_trajectory: Copilot opened PR with initial optimization attempt.
Boshen and Dunqing quickly provided feedback: complete removal might be feasible, and const arrays should be static.
Copilot removed validation entirely, then after Dunqing's rejection, implemented pattern-based validation.
After several rounds of feedback on rebasing and unifying Jest/Vitest, the PR was eventually closed without merge.
